column1: # The link between the bridge Pico and the PC is "$<len>,<crc16>,<payload>\n". Three
# implementations decode it, and a disagreement means the ground station drops frames the
# bridge sent or accepts frames it did not:
# They already agreed on what a valid frame is. They did not agree on what a broken one is:
# an oversized length field was an "overflow" in C++ and a generic "resync" in the other
# two, so the same corruption produced different diagnostics depending on which end an
# operator was reading. This file settles that, and every other recovery rule with it.
# Format: <id> TAB <input bytes, hex> TAB <expected events> TAB <expected counters>
# Events are comma-separated "<kind>:<payload hex>", in order, where kind is ok or crc.
# An empty field means the decoder must produce nothing. Counters are the decoder's totals
# after the whole input has been fed, and they are exact: a decoder that reaches the right
# frames by the wrong route still fails.
